OPERATOR_CORRECTION.claim_assigned_to_me: Linode accepts PayPal and Google Pay, so it is a good card-failure fallback.
OPERATOR_CORRECTION.THE_MISTAKE_THAT_CAUSED_IT: I checked payment METHODS, regions, specs and price — and never checked which COUNTRIES Akamai supports for billing. That is a gate that invalidates everything downstream of it, and I put it last instead of first. Country acceptance is now gate #1 for any provider, before specs, before price.
OPERATOR_CORRECTION.note: The operator's direct experience outranks a search result. My PayPal finding was true and irrelevant — a method that cannot be attached to a Nigeria-billed account does not exist.

ROOT_CAUSE_FOUND.finding: THE CARD IS THE CONSTRAINT, NOT THE PROVIDER.

evidence.statement: 'Verve cards are not accepted by AWS.' Stated as unconditional, regardless of funding or currency.
Rejects Verve, rejects Nigerian naira BINs at the network level, AND officially rejects prepaid/virtual credit cards — which is precisely the workaround Nigerians reach for.
'Nigerian banks responded by capping international transactions at $20-100/month on most debit cards.' A $152 run exceeds a typical cap even when the card is otherwise valid.
'flag new accounts... certain African IP ranges'. Legitimate accounts are rejected on IP/device signals regardless of card validity.

the_variant_that_matters.finding: Verve comes in two versions and they behave completely differently internationally.
the_variant_that_matters.Verve Classic: domestic-only. Commonly rejected at international checkouts. Will not work on ANY cloud provider.
the_variant_that_matters.Verve Global: runs on Discover's international network. 'Has a real shot at going through.'
the_variant_that_matters.actionable: If the operator has a Verve card, their bank can confirm in a minute which variant it is. If Classic, the card is the entire problem and no provider change helps.

the_actual_fix.solution: A USD-denominated VIRTUAL DOLLAR CARD funded in NGN or USDT. It presents to the merchant as a normal international Visa/Mastercard, while the funding leg stays local — so the bank international-spend cap does not apply.
the_actual_fix.typical_cost: USD 100 of compute costs USD 103-108 after creation fee, conversion fee and FX markup.
the_actual_fix.why_this_is_the highest-leverage_finding: It makes the PROVIDER CHOICE LARGELY IRRELEVANT. With a working USD virtual card, Azure, DigitalOcean, Kamatera, Linode and Oracle all open. Without one, none of them do. We have been solving a payment problem by shopping for compute.

FREE_OPTIONS_SCORED_AGAINST_OUR_ACTUAL_C.binding_constraint: megacmd IGNORES the '::' subpath and fetches the ENTIRE 319.95 GB share, so the VM must stage all of it. ~350 GB needed.

FREE_OPTIONS_SCORED_AGAINST_OUR_ACTUAL_C.conclusion: There is NO genuinely free option that fits today. Every 'free' tier that exists is between 10x and 300x too small on disk, and every one of them that is big enough still requires a card that is being declined.

THE_LEVER_THAT_WOULD_CHANGE_THE_ANSWER.observation: The 350 GB requirement is an ARTEFACT of megacmd ignoring '::' subpaths, not a property of the corpus. It is the single constraint eliminating every free option.
THE_LEVER_THAT_WOULD_CHANGE_THE_ANSWER.hypothesis: megacmd's '::' path syntax is designed for a REAL SESSION. Anonymous access works for a whole-share get but not for subpath addressing — consistent with 'mega-ls' returning 'Not logged in' on a public link while 'mega-get' succeeded anonymously on the same link.
THE_LEVER_THAT_WOULD_CHANGE_THE_ANSWER.test: Create a FREE MEGA account, log megacmd in on the VM, import the public link into that account's session, then retry single-file '::' addressing.
THE_LEVER_THAT_WOULD_CHANGE_THE_ANSWER.cost: $0. MEGA free accounts are free and instant.
THE_LEVER_THAT_WOULD_CHANGE_THE_ANSWER.if_it_works: Peak disk drops from ~350 GB to ~4 GB (one file at a time, deleted after transcription). THAT WOULD QUALIFY: Google Cloud's free e2-micro (30 GB), Oracle Always Free (200 GB, 50x oversized), Kamatera's trial, and any $5/mo VPS. The free tier becomes reachable.
THE_LEVER_THAT_WOULD_CHANGE_THE_ANSWER.if_it_fails: Nothing changes. The 350 GB constraint stands and we pay for disk, as currently planned.
THE_LEVER_THAT_WOULD_CHANGE_THE_ANSWER.status: UNTESTED. This is the highest-value untested hypothesis in the project.
THE_LEVER_THAT_WOULD_CHANGE_THE_ANSWER.why_it_is_cheap_to_test: It needs a free account and one megacmd command. It does not touch the corpus, does not download bytes, and does not cost money.

RECOMMENDATION_ORDER: 1. CHECK THE CARD VARIANT. If Verve Classic, no provider will work and the virtual dollar card is mandatory. If Verve Global, Azure may work today.
2. TEST THE MEGA-SESSION HYPOTHESIS. It is free, fast, and it is what actually decides whether a free tier is reachable.
3. ONLY THEN CHOOSE A PROVIDER. With the card sorted and the disk requirement known, Azure at ~$26 becomes a $26 decision rather than a gamble.
